title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Delamination Detection on 5D Analyzer
subtitle: Pre-Diffusion Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Thomas Mueller

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the 5D Analyzer system to detect and classify Delamination defects during pre-diffusion inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab A to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Delamination defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the 5D Analyzer platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: 5D Analyzer
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Delamination
- Process Step: Pre-Diffusion
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab A

This test case applies to all 5D Analyzer systems deployed at Milpitas Fab A for pre-diffusion monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: 5D Analyzer
Software Version: v9.6.975
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_14nm_PRE_DIFFUSION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (171 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the 5D Analyzer system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Delamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 95 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 97% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.2% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-06-24
Wafers Tested: 28
Total Defects Found: 2510
Defect Density: 798.96 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.4%
Capture Rate: 99.8%
Test Duration: 122 minutes
System Uptime: 99.1%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The 5D Analyzer demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Delamination at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) Statistical process control charts showed stable performance over the test period.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
